title: Scientists find closest star to the Milky Way's central black hole
gist: Researchers using ESO's GRAVITY instrument discovered S301, the closest known star to the Milky Way's central black hole Sgr A*, whose orbital precession could yield the first-ever measurement of the black hole's spin within about a decade.

insights.claim: Researchers using the GRAVITY instrument at the European Southern Observatory's Very Large Telescope discovered a star, S301, orbiting closer to the Milky Way's central black hole Sgr A* than any previously known star, with an 8.7-year orbital period and an extreme eccentricity of 0.9832.
insights.speaker: John Timmer
insights.so_what: A pure scientific and instrumentation development, not directly investable, but a proof point for ground-based interferometry as a lower-cost alternative to space telescopes for extreme-precision astrophysics.
insights.locator: In Wednesday's issue of Nature, researchers describe a recently discovered star

insights.claim: Researchers estimate that roughly a decade of continued tracking of S301's orbital precession could yield the first-ever measurement of Sgr A*'s spin, a fundamental black-hole property that has never been directly measured despite decades of study.
insights.speaker: John Timmer
insights.so_what: Identifies a concrete near-term milestone in fundamental astrophysics that could be a signpost for continued institutional funding and interest in VLT/GRAVITY-class instrumentation.
insights.locator: the researchers estimate that we already have instruments that can track S301's orbit

insights.claim: At its closest approach, S301 moves at about 25,000 kilometers per second -- over 8 percent of the speed of light -- passing roughly 10 times closer to Sgr A* than the previously closest-known star, at a distance of as little as 11 Astronomical Units.
insights.speaker: John Timmer
insights.so_what: Quantifies just how extreme this newly discovered orbit is relative to prior observations, underscoring why it is a uniquely valuable natural probe of the black hole.
insights.locator: the star is moving at about 25,000 kilometers a second
